title: KS Drift Detector with Bonferroni Correction
hints: Drop None values first. A null is a missing measurement, not a zero.
The empirical CDFs only change at sample points, so the supremum is attained at one of the values in either sample. Check the union, not just the reference.
Compare |a*m - b*n| as integers to find D and its first location, then divide by n*m.
Bonferroni divides alpha by the number of features you actually tested, not by every column in the schema.
